Elena — thanks for the clear questions and the annotated PDF. Looping in Irene (KMS onboarding) and Monica (secops) to provide the technical evidence and operational controls. Quick summary answers up front, followed by schedule proposals.

Summary up front:
- Import methods: we support HSM vendor-signed wrapped imports (PKCS#7/PKCS#11 wrapped envelopes where supported by the HSM vendor), KMIP and signed-key-import flows, and an offline import option (sealed, encrypted transfer with chain-of-custody via courier).
- Retention: Redwood never stores key plaintext. We retain wrapped key envelopes + metadata (import time, key-id, import method) and full immutable audit logs (who/when/operation).
- Rotation: flexible — we support customer-managed rotation APIs and automated rotation with configurable cadence. Rollback: we retain previous wrapped key versions until customer triggers zeroization; we surface version history and can perform controlled rollbacks if the customer allows it in policy.
- TLS/mTLS: management APIs support TLS 1.2/1.3 with a recommended cipher list; we support mTLS for customer management plane connections and can accommodate client cert provisioning.

Action items / proposed next steps:
1) Irene will send a detailed technical note with supported import formats, key-wrapping algorithms, and courier handling checklist.
2) We'll provide a redline-friendly SOW and onboarding checklist (attaching Redwood_BYO_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx and a key handshake diagram).
3) Proposed sync: Thu Jun 17 10:00AM ET — 30m to cover handover, acceptance criteria, and timeline. Does that work?

Attaching: redwood_key_handshake_diagram.png (handshake + envelope flow), Redwood_BYO_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx

Thanks,

Subject: Re: BYO key handover approach — a few clarifying questions

Hi Elena — good to meet virtually in a few minutes. I promised the technical note; below is a concise set of specifics we will expand in the follow-up doc and in the drive folder.

1) Supported import methods (details):
- Vendor-signed import (preferred): we support HSM vendor-signed import envelopes (PKCS#7 / CMS wrappers or vendor-specific signed blobs). For Thales and Entrust we have validated flows for importing wrapped key material directly into our HSM-backed key vault.
- KMIP: for key provisioning we support KMIP v1.2 and v2.0 (depending on partner gateway).
- PKCS#11: supported for direct HSM operations where the customer supplies an HSM connected to our private deployment (Private mode).
- Offline sealed import: customer provides an encrypted export (AES-GCM wrapped), shipped via courier with chain-of-custody. Redwood performs import in a secure room with two-person auth and tamper-evident handling; operator names and timestamps recorded in the audit log.

2) What we retain: 
- We never persist plaintext key material in long-term storage. On import we keep: (a) the wrapped key envelope (binary), (b) import metadata (key id, algorithm, bits, import method, import operator), and (c) full, immutable audit events (who/what/when).
- We retain transient in-memory material only for the duration necessary to load into the HSM; this executes inside an isolated kernel module and is zeroed immediately upon HSM ingestion. We provide a signed attestation of zeroization steps on request (SOC/assessment redaction as required).

3) Rotation and rollback behavior: 
- Rotation models: automatic (platform-managed) with configurable cadence (30/90/180 days) OR customer-managed API-triggered rotation.
- Rollback: we maintain versioned wrapped keys; rollback is allowed but gated by policy: if rollback is initiated we perform a safe-cache-drain where ephemeral inference KV caches are flushed and a short grace period is enforced to invalidate existing sessions. For high-throughput low-latency customers we recommend a blue/green key roll where the runtime accepts both old/new wrapped keys for a brief coexistence window (controlled by the customer policy).
- Emergency zeroization: can be triggered by customer or Redwood with documented escrow/approval flows. Zeroization is propagated to all replicas; we record signed audit artifacts.

4) TLS / mTLS details:
- TLS: TLS 1.2 (recommended minimum) and 1.3 supported. Recommended cipher suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256, ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256. We will provide the full IANA list in the drive doc.
- mTLS: supported. Client cert formats: PEM and P12 (PKCS#12). Certificate provisioning can be automated via ACME (customer managed) or manual upload.

5) Cache / in-flight request handling:
- We maintain an explicit KV cache with per-key TTL and eviction hooks. During rotation we: (a) mark old key as deprecated, (b) drain caches (TTL-based) and optionally force flush via API, (c) apply blue/green acceptance if requested. We provide logs that show cache-drain events and token invalidations.

6) HSM operator and compatibility:
- Redwood provides trained import operators for Hosted and Dedicated customers. For Private deployments the customer may provide an on-site operator; Redwood provides runbook and remote witness options. Compatibility validated with Thales Luna N, Entrust nShield, and Safenet models — we will include exact firmware versions in the validation matrix.

Attachments / follow-up: I'll drop the full technical appendix to the Drive folder (see link) and upload the chain-of-custody template and the operator manifest.

Regards,
Irene Choi
